statement: Let n = len(heights). Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n and r is the final level array defined by the following sequential process. Initialize w^0_i = 0 for every i with 0 <= i < n. For each t = 0,1,...,volume-1, let L^t_i = heights[i] + w^t_i. Define the next index j_t as follows. Let a be the smallest index with 0 <= a <= k such that L^t_k >= L^t_{k-1} >= ... >= L^t_a (this chain is vacuous if a = k) and either a = 0 or L^t_{a-1} > L^t_a. Let m_L = min { L^t_i : a <= i <= k }. If m_L < L^t_k, let j_L be the largest index i with a <= i <= k and L^t_i = m_L. If m_L < L^t_k, set j_t = j_L. Otherwise, let b be the largest index with k <= b < n such that L^t_k >= L^t_{k+1} >= ... >= L^t_b (this chain is vacuous if b = k) and either b = n-1 or L^t_{b+1} > L^t_b. Let m_R = min { L^t_i : k <= i <= b }. If m_R < L^t_k, let j_R be the smallest index i with k <= i <= b and L^t_i = m_R. If m_R < L^t_k, set j_t = j_R. If neither left nor right case applies, set j_t = k. Then set w^{t+1}_i = w^t_i + 1 if i = j_t, and w^{t+1}_i = w^t_i otherwise. Finally, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = heights[i] + w^{volume}_i.

Define the sequence O of length n by O_t = k - t for 0 <= t <= k, and O_t = t for k < t < n. Then whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = c + q + (1 if there exists t with 0 <= t < rmd and O_t = i, else 0).
